messages:
marta: Customer in eu-west reported intermittent 503s to their private API right after our scheduled cert rotation at 03:00 UTC. Only requests coming from their app subnet fail, other clients are fine. They see TLS errors in their logs. Any quick checks?

jamie: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro (client side curl / s_client) and DNS results from their subnet? Is this persistent or flapping?

marta: Quick outputs from their side:

```
$ dig +short api.customer.internal
10.10.120.45
10.10.121.99
$ dig +nocmd +noall +answer api.customer.internal @10.10.1.2
api.customer.internal. 3600 IN A 10.10.120.45
api.customer.internal. 3600 IN A 10.10.121.99
```

marta: They said 10.10.121.99 started returning 503/TLS handshake failures right after rotation. TTL shows 3600 but app instances keep old VIP pinned in some AZs.

ana: Can you run an openssl check from a failing host against the problematic VIP with SNI? Example: `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.121.99:443 -servername api.customer.internal -showcerts`

marta: They ran it, output excerpt:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = example-root
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.customer.internal
   i:/CN=redwood-rotated-2026
 1 s:/CN=redwood-rotated-2026
   i:/CN=example-root
---
SSL handshake has read 4567 bytes and written 345 bytes
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

jamie: Interesting — the VIP is returning only the leaf cert, not the full chain. Some of the client stacks will still accept that if they can fetch intermediates, but with our private deployment they can't reach public AIA endpoints. Could be a chain not published to the edge proxy instance for that VIP.

lee: Also double-check egress allowlist: if the proxy is configured to OCSP staple and cannot reach OCSP responders from that subnet, strict clients might fail handshake. Can you confirm outbound 80/443 to the CA endpoints from the edge node?

marta: Edge node (10.10.121.99) egress test: `curl -I https://ocsp.exampleca.com` returns connection timed out. Their FW policy blocks outbound to public OCSP/CRL.

ana: OK two issues stacking: (1) rotated cert omitted intermediates on that edge VM, (2) the edge cannot fetch OCSP/CRL so no stapling -> some clients reject. Repro steps I ran locally:

```
# simulating the broken chain
openssl s_server -accept 443 -cert leaf.pem -key leaf.key -no_chain
# client fails if it can't retrieve issuer
openssl s_client -connect localhost:443 -servername api.customer.internal -verify_return_error
```

jamie: Short-term mitigation: push the full bundle (leaf + intermediates) to the edge instance for 10.10.121.99 and restart the proxy process (no global redeploy). Also add a temporary egress rule allowing ocsp.exampleca.com for that edge. That should fix handshakes immediately.

deploy-bot: deploy started: push-cert/edge/10.10.121.99 -> user jamie triggered at 2187654380.

lee: When you push, verify `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.121.99:443 -servername api.customer.internal -status` shows OCSP response stapled and chain present. Expected output lines: `OCSP response: no response` -> BAD, `OCSP Response Status: successful` -> GOOD.

marta: Jamies' push finished, restarted proxy. Quick checks from the customer's app:
- curl now returns 200
- openssl s_client shows chain and OCSP stapled

marta: Customer confirmed: traffic recovered in the failing AZ, they flushed local DNS cache and restarted a few app pods. They left TTL as 3600 but we'll coordinate a shorter TTL for future rotations. :thumbsup:

ana: Action items: 1) Add certificate bundle validation to rotation job so every edge gets leaf+intermediates 2) Add preflight egress test for OCSP endpoints before marking rotation complete 3) Recommend customers set lower DNS TTL around rotation windows.

jamie: I'll file a follow-up ticket to make the rotation job stricter and add the OCSP preflight (link in ticket). Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
